title: FDA vs EMA Pivotal Trial Design: Comparators, Primary Endpoints and Estimands
summary: Where FDA and EMA diverge on comparators, primary endpoints, single-trial evidence and estimands, and how precedents shape one pivotal program for both agencies.
body_markdown:
## FDA vs EMA pivotal trial design: where expectations diverge on comparators, endpoints and estimands


FDA and EMA work from the same ICH statistical framework: E9(R1) for estimands, E10 for control groups and E17 for multi-regional trials. Their written guidance and their decisions on individual products still differ in four predictable places:


- **Comparator.** FDA asks whether the drug works, which in many indications means placebo-controlled evidence, though FDA accepts other controls where appropriate. In many indications, EMA also asks how the drug compares with established treatment. That often means an active-controlled or three-arm study.
- **Weight of evidence.** Both agencies accept a single pivotal trial. EMA states the bar in statistical terms ("considerably stronger than p<0.05"). FDA frames it as one trial plus confirmatory evidence.
- **Uncontrolled and surrogate-based evidence.** FDA has repeatedly approved products on single-arm response rates or biomarker surrogates. In comparable cases, CHMP refused the same products.
- **Clinical relevance of the primary endpoint.** In Alzheimer's disease and geographic atrophy, FDA accepted an integrated scale (Alzheimer's) or a lesion-growth slope analysis (geographic atrophy) as supporting approval. CHMP questioned whether the effect mattered to patients. In early Alzheimer's disease, Leqembi and Kisunla were authorised in the EU only after re-examination and only for ApoE4 non-carriers and heterozygotes. In geographic atrophy, Syfovre was refused.


On estimands the two agencies have largely converged. Both favour a treatment-policy approach for treatment discontinuation, and both expect data to be collected after discontinuation. EMA guidance is more prescriptive, intercurrent event by intercurrent event.


The sections below set out the guidance positions, the precedents that show them in practice, and the design features that have let one program satisfy both agencies.


---


### 1. Shared foundation: what ICH already harmonises


The divergences sit on top of a common vocabulary, so it helps to be clear about what is already aligned.


- **Control groups (ICH E10).** E10 explains what each design can show. It explicitly does *not* set regional regulatory requirements[402](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=402) . It notes that the active comparator should generally be acceptable in the region where the application is submitted[417](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=417) , and that placebo-controlled trials may be more or less acceptable across ICH regions[418](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=418) . A three-arm design (test, active, placebo) gives internal evidence of assay sensitivity. It also lets a sponsor tell an ineffective drug apart from a trial that could not detect an effect[414](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=414) .
- **Estimands (ICH E9(R1)).** The addendum defines the estimand attributes and five strategies for intercurrent events: treatment policy, hypothetical, composite, while-on-treatment and principal stratum[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=94)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=101) . It presents the framework as a tool for sponsor–regulator dialogue[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=108) . It expects the estimand to be agreed iteratively, early in planning[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=111) .
- **Multi-regional trials (ICH E17).** E17 sets the standard of a *single* primary analysis approach, agreed before the trial starts. Where scientific or regulatory differences justify different analyses, these should be described in the protocol and covered by one integrated statistical analysis plan[571](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=571) . Comparators should "in principle be the same across participating regions" and should be agreed with the relevant authorities[572](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=572) .


The practical consequence is that FDA and EMA rarely ask for a different *framework* . They ask for different *content* within it.


---


### 2. Comparator choice


#### FDA: effectiveness, not comparative effectiveness


FDA guidance separates showing that a drug works from showing that it is as good as existing therapy. E10, as adopted by FDA, states that superiority to an active comparator is not needed and that, depending on the situation, non-inferiority may not be needed either[303](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=303) . FDA's non-inferiority guidance makes the same point: a drug can meet the effectiveness standard by beating placebo without supporting any conclusion that it is "as effective or even nearly as effective" as an active comparator[304](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=304) . Comparative labeling claims carry a higher bar. A claim of similar effectiveness needs a non-inferiority margin tighter than the one that merely establishes effectiveness[316](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=316) .


Indication-specific FDA guidance follows the same logic:


- **Type 2 diabetes (2023 draft).** Depending on the design, either non-inferiority to an active comparator (with a justified margin) or superiority to placebo or an active comparator may be appropriate[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=67) .
- **Obesity (2025 draft).** Phase 3 trials should generally be randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, on a background of diet and exercise[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=460) .
- **MDD (2018 draft).** A placebo group is necessary. Non-inferiority designs cannot establish antidepressant efficacy because of high placebo response[461](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=461)[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=477) .


#### EMA: placebo where ethical, plus an active comparator where benefit–risk needs context


CHMP's 2011 reflection paper on the need for active control sets the EU position:


- Include placebo where it is ethical and feasible.
- Expect comparisons against *both* placebo and an active control in certain indications.
- When an active comparator is required, it is usually the EU-licensed gold-standard product[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=351)[366](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=366) .


The paper says a three-arm trial "will often be required" when non-inferiority to an active treatment is the objective, because placebo superiority is the most compelling evidence of assay sensitivity[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=371) . It also notes that adding an active arm does not automatically require a fully powered non-inferiority test[349](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=349) .


Disease-specific EMA guidelines put this into practice:


Indication (EMA guideline) EMA comparator expectation Contrast with FDA guidance


Type 2 diabetes (Rev. 2, 2024) Placebo-controlled monotherapy is "always required," even for an add-on-only claim[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=23) . At least one active-controlled non-inferiority study against standard of care is recommended, with a 0.3% HbA1c margin[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=22) . FDA presents placebo superiority *or* active-control non-inferiority as alternatives, depending on design[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=67) .


Depression (Rev. 3, 2025) Placebo is required in at least one study, and at least two pivotal short-term studies are required[547](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=547) . Active-comparator superiority can count as one of the two[548](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=548) . Non-inferiority cannot be the sole basis for efficacy[549](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=549) . FDA agrees that non-inferiority cannot establish antidepressant efficacy[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=477) .


Schizophrenia (Rev. 1, 2013) For non-inferiority, a three-arm trial with placebo is recommended[378](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=378) .


Insomnia (Rev. 1, 2011) Three-arm studies are "strongly recommended"[377](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=377) .


#### Precedent: the SURPASS model


The tirzepatide (Mounjaro) type 2 diabetes program shows how one portfolio met both positions. It ran five global phase 3 trials:


- Two were double-blind and placebo-controlled: SURPASS-1 and SURPASS-5.
- Three were open-label and active-controlled: semaglutide 1 mg (SURPASS-2), insulin degludec (SURPASS-3) and insulin glargine (SURPASS-4)[853](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=853)[855](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=855) .


FDA's review lists the same comparator set[654](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=654) . The placebo trials met the FDA-style effectiveness standard and EMA's monotherapy placebo requirement. The active-controlled trials gave EMA its comparison with standard of care. One set of five shared pivotal trials covered both applications.


---


### 3. How much evidence: one pivotal trial


Both agencies accept a single pivotal trial, but they describe the threshold differently.


- **FDA.** The 1998 guidance set the general expectation of at least two adequate and well-controlled studies[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=203) . The 2023 draft on one trial plus confirmatory evidence weighs quality and quantity together: a highly persuasive trial needs less confirmatory evidence[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=179) . The 2026 draft on substantial evidence of effectiveness says the single-trial approach generally involves either a highly persuasive trial or strong confirmatory evidence, and should be discussed with FDA *before* the trial starts[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=176) . That draft will replace the 1998 guidance only when finalized[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=205) .
- **EMA.** The points-to-consider on single pivotal studies call such applications exceptional and requiring an "exceptionally compelling" study[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=269)[270](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=270) . The study needs statistical evidence "considerably stronger than p<0.05," narrow confidence intervals, internal consistency across subgroups and no dominant centre[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=274)[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=275)[276](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=276) .


**Design implication.** If a global program depends on one pivotal trial, size it so the expected result clears EMA's stricter significance and precision bar. FDA's confirmatory-evidence route does not on its own satisfy CHMP.


---


### 4. Uncontrolled designs and surrogate endpoints: the sharpest divergence


#### Guidance positions


- **FDA.** FDA's oncology endpoints guidance calls ORR "the most commonly used surrogate endpoint supporting accelerated approval." It says single-arm trials in refractory tumors can assess ORR accurately[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=171) . The 2023 draft on single-arm trials for accelerated approval confirms response rate as the usual endpoint and recommends discussing appropriateness with FDA[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=173) .
- **EMA.** The CHMP reflection paper on single-arm trials as pivotal evidence (adopted 9 September 2024) treats RCTs as the standard[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=522)[528](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=528) . Applicants must justify departing from that standard[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=523) . The paper's reasoning is that without randomisation, effect estimates depend on assumptions that cannot be tested[530](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=530) . The older anticancer guideline (Revision 3, 2006) went further: "without further justification, ORR is not an acceptable primary endpoint" in confirmatory trials[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=128) .


#### Precedents where the outcomes split


Product FDA outcome and design basis CHMP outcome and design objections


**Folotyn (pralatrexate), relapsed/refractory PTCL** Accelerated approval on 24 September 2009, based on ORR (27%) from PROPEL, a single-arm phase 2 trial[1141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1141)[1161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1161)[1164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1164) Negative opinion on 19 January 2012, confirmed after re-examination on 19 April 2012[1075](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1075) . CHMP noted the single-arm design went against EMA protocol advice[1077](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1077) . Without a comparator, the size of the response could not be judged[1078](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1078) . Response rate had not been accepted as a registration endpoint[1079](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1079) .


**Gamifant (emapalumab), primary HLH** Regular approval on 20 November 2018 on a single-arm phase 2/3 study (ORR 63%). FDA judged an RCT impracticable[1126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1126)[1134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1134)[1137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1137)[1138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1138) Refused. Grounds: emapalumab's effect could not be separated from concomitant therapy and the variable disease course[969](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=969) . CHMP considered an RCT of about 85 to 110 patients feasible[973](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=973) . The new ORR definition had unclear clinical relevance[974](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=974) . Starting new HLH treatment was not counted as non-response[976](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=976) .


**Exondys 51 (eteplirsen), DMD** Accelerated approval on 19 September 2016, with increased dystrophin accepted as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit[1098](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1098)[1100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1100) . FDA reviewers found the clinical studies did not give substantial evidence of effectiveness[1103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1103) . Negative opinion on 31 May 2018, confirmed on 20 September 2018[906](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=906) . Grounds: no placebo-controlled data beyond 24 weeks[907](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=907) ; external controls that were non-concurrent and selected post hoc[910](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=910) ; and the view that dystrophin correlation cannot replace a controlled confirmatory trial[914](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=914) .


**Elevidys (delandistrogene moxeparvovec), DMD** Accelerated approval on 22 June 2023, with micro-dystrophin expression at Week 12 as the surrogate[943](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=943)[944](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=944) . In the later EMBARK trial, the primary NSAA endpoint did not reach significance (difference 0.65, p=0.244)[950](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=950) . EPAR refusal. CHMP considered micro-dystrophin at best a pharmacodynamic marker, with no established surrogacy[989](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=989) .


**Lesson.** EMA has not objected to placebo-controlled pivotal designs (as with Elevidys's EMBARK[986](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=986) ). It refused Elevidys on the result, not the design: EMBARK did not show an effect on movement abilities at 12 months. What it has resisted is an efficacy conclusion that depends on a single-arm response rate, an external control or a biomarker that has not been validated as a surrogate. If an FDA accelerated-approval strategy uses those elements, the EU dossier needs a randomized confirmatory trial built into the global plan from the start, not added afterwards.


---


### 5. Primary endpoints and clinical relevance


#### Alzheimer's disease: co-primary vs integrated scale


- **EMA (2018 guideline, Revision 2).** For mild to moderate AD dementia, the cognitive effect should be clinically meaningful. Its relevance should be confirmed by a functional or global endpoint in a **co-primary** approach[694](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=694)[695](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=695) . In prodromal AD, two co-primaries "may be difficult," but clinical relevance must still be shown[697](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=697) .
- **FDA (2024 draft).** "An integrated scale that adequately and meaningfully assesses independent effects on both daily function and cognition is also acceptable as a single primary efficacy outcome measure in early AD patients"[687](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=687) .


The two anti-amyloid antibodies show what this difference means in practice.


- **Leqembi (lecanemab).** The primary endpoint was CDR-SB at 18 months: −0.45 vs placebo in FAS+, −0.39 in the FDA FAS population[802](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=802) .


- **FDA** found this a clinically meaningful reduction in decline and converted the product to traditional approval[803](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=803)[782](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=782) .
- **CHMP** first judged the effect small. The neurology SAG considered it not clinically relevant[824](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=824)[825](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=825) , and the initial procedure ended with grounds for refusal[827](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=827) .
- **Outcome in the EU.** On re-examination, the indication excluded ApoE4 homozygotes[828](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=828) . CHMP then concluded benefit–risk was favourable in non-carriers and heterozygotes, with additional risk minimisation[830](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=830) . Authorisation followed on 15 April 2025[814](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=814) .


- **Kisunla (donanemab).** The primary endpoint was iADRS at Week 76, with CDR-SB as a key secondary[1012](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1012) . During the transition from phase 2 to phase 3, the primary endpoint had been changed from CDR-SB to iADRS[1014](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1014) .


- **FDA** first questioned whether the composite reflected benefit on both cognition and function. Significant effects on both component scales and on CDR-SB resolved the concern. FDA cautioned that this did not establish iADRS for other programs[1193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1193)[1194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1194)[1195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1195) .
- **CHMP** noted that the observed differences (2.52 and 1.58 points) were below the sponsor's own 3.2-point clinically important difference, and that clinical relevance was "not sufficiently substantiated"[1016](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1016)[1017](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1017) .
- **Outcome in the EU.** A majority recommendation for ApoE4 non-carriers and heterozygotes came only at re-examination, with dissenting views recorded[1021](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1021)[1022](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1022) . EU marketing authorisation followed on 24 September 2025, restricted to that population.


**Lesson.** For EMA, a statistically significant integrated-scale result is necessary but not sufficient. Sponsors should prespecify and protect, under multiplicity control, the separate cognitive and functional components, and should support the clinically important difference with evidence that is not drawn from their own phase 2 data.


#### Geographic atrophy: anatomical endpoint without functional benefit


- **FDA (Syfovre).** For pegcetacoplan, FDA accepted the rate of GA lesion growth (slope) as the primary endpoint, in preference to the protocol's Month-12 change[883](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=883)[884](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=884) . Its reasoning was that a slower growth rate would eventually produce a clinically significant effect[882](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=882) .
- **CHMP.** CHMP accepted lesion size as a primary outcome in principle[1053](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1053) . It still concluded that slower lesion growth had not translated into meaningful visual-function benefit at 24 months[1052](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1052) , and that no clinical benefit outweighed the risks[1047](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1047) . CHMP confirmed its negative opinion on re-examination on 19 September 2024, and marketing authorisation was refused on 16 December 2024.


**Lesson.** Where the endpoint is anatomical or a biomarker, EMA expects a patient-relevant functional effect within the trial period, or a convincing argument that one will follow. Visual-function endpoints therefore need to be powered as key secondaries, not just collected.


#### Oncology


FDA treats OS, PFS and ORR as context-dependent. PFS can be a direct benefit, a surrogate for traditional approval or a surrogate for accelerated approval[165](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=165)[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=166) . The EMA guidance text cited here is older (Revision 3, 2006). It ties the choice of OS as primary endpoint to the toxicity balance and to whether effective next-line therapy exists[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=127) . Later EMA material (Revision 6, 2024) accepts EFS or PFS in non-inferiority substitution designs. Where toxicity increases, it requires large gains in EFS, PFS or OS[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=129)[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=130) . Sponsors should check the current EMA anticancer guideline revision directly. The core difference remains EMA's reluctance to accept ORR as a confirmatory primary endpoint.


#### Metabolic indications: largely aligned


- **Diabetes.** Both agencies use HbA1c as the primary endpoint[19](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=19)[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=65) . FDA advises against using responder analyses as the primary HbA1c analysis[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=71) .
- **Obesity.** EMA (2017) uses weight reduction as the primary endpoint, with responder analyses at ≥5% and ≥10% at 12 months[440](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=440)[441](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=441) . FDA's 2025 draft uses mean percentage change in body weight[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=456) . Wegovy's STEP 1 to 3 trials used both as co-primaries: percentage change and ≥5% responders[675](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=675) .
- **Power cost of co-primaries.** FDA's multiple endpoints guidance notes that two independent co-primaries, each powered at 80%, give about 64% joint power[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=606) .

### 6. Estimands: convergence on treatment policy, with differences in detail


#### Guidance positions


**FDA**


- **Obesity (2025 draft).** Trials should generally include a treatment-policy estimand, with subjects measured at every visit regardless of intercurrent events unless they withdraw consent[634](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=634) . Alternatives must address a meaningful clinical question under plausible assumptions[636](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=636) .
- **Diabetes (2023 draft).** Rescue medication and dose changes should be documented as intercurrent events and accounted for in the analysis. The draft does not prescribe a strategy and refers to E9(R1)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=69)[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=70) .


**EMA**


- **Diabetes (2024).** EMA specifies a strategy for each event. Treatment discontinuation should be handled with treatment policy[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=27) . Rescue medication may be handled with a hypothetical strategy, with suitable modelling[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=28) . Non-inferiority trials need conservative estimation and probably a supplementary estimand[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=29) .
- **Depression (2025).** Treatment policy is the default for discontinuation "unless an alternative strategy is duly justified"[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=334) . A hypothetical full-adherence estimand is of interest "as a secondary estimand only"[336](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=336) .
- **Alzheimer's (2018).** The effect regardless of discontinuation is "normally an appropriate strategy" for the primary target[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=339) .
- **Oncology crossover (Q&A, December 2018).** Hypothetical "no-crossover" OS adjustments can only be supportive or sensitivity analyses. They cannot rescue a trial that is otherwise negative[502](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=502)[500](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=500) .


#### Precedents


- **Wegovy (EMA).** Treatment policy was the protocol-defined primary estimand. All superiority claims rested on it[678](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=678) . The "trial product" hypothetical estimand was secondary[679](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=679) . CHMP called the treatment-policy approach "conservative and acceptable" and accepted retrieved-dropout multiple imputation[682](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=682)[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=684) .
- **Wegovy (FDA).** The FDA review shows the same retrieved-dropout imputation approach[733](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=733) .
- **Mounjaro.** SURPASS reported an "efficacy" estimand (hypothetical, on-treatment) and a "treatment-regimen" estimand[857](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=857) . FDA's statistical review analysed all available data regardless of adherence or rescue[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=655) . In the later weight-management variation, CHMP called the treatment-regimen estimand "more relevant for regulatory decision-making"[858](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=858) .


**Lesson.** For one global program, the lowest-risk approach has three parts:


1. Use treatment policy for discontinuation as the primary estimand.
2. Build data collection after discontinuation into protocols and consent forms (FDA recommends exactly this[638](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=638)[641](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=641) ).
3. Prespecify hypothetical or on-treatment estimands as supplementary.


Rescue medication is where the agencies may differ in a given indication: EMA's diabetes guideline accepts a hypothetical strategy. That difference fits E17's mechanism of region-specific analyses described in the protocol and covered by one integrated SAP[571](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=571) .

### 7. Designing one development program for both agencies


#### Use parallel scientific advice early


The EMA–FDA parallel scientific advice program is intended to increase dialogue and help the agencies converge on development requirements. Each agency still gives independent advice[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=232) . Requests should preferably line up with an FDA pre-IND or End-of-Phase 2 meeting[239](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=239) . The advice can differ, so sponsors should treat it as a way to find disagreements early, not as a single joint opinion[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=241) . The precedents above show why this matters. Folotyn's pivotal single-arm design went against CHMP protocol advice[1077](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1077) . Gamifant's endpoints were amended mid-study after an interim look[978](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=978) .


#### Design checklist drawn from guidance and precedent


Design element Choice that has worked for both agencies Basis


Comparator Combine placebo-controlled trials (for FDA effectiveness and EU assay sensitivity) with at least one active-controlled trial against the EU standard of care, or use a three-arm design. Keep the comparator the same across regions. EMA reflection paper[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=351)[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=371) ; SURPASS[853](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=853) ; E17[572](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=572)


Number and strength of trials Plan two pivotal trials. If only one, size it to give evidence well beyond p<0.05 with narrow confidence intervals. EMA[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=274) ; FDA[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=176)[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=179)


Uncontrolled evidence Do not rely on single-arm, external-control or unvalidated-surrogate efficacy for the EU. Run a randomized confirmatory trial in parallel. EMA reflection paper on single-arm trials[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=523)[530](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=530) ; Folotyn, Gamifant, Exondys refusals[1078](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1078)[969](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=969)[914](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=914)


Primary endpoint Choose the endpoint that meets the stricter clinical-relevance test. Where FDA accepts an integrated or anatomical endpoint, make the EU-preferred functional or component endpoints key secondaries under multiplicity control, and justify the MCID with outside evidence. EMA AD guideline[694](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=694) ; Kisunla[1016](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1016)[1194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1194) ; Syfovre[1052](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=1052)


Co-primaries Budget sample size for joint power. FDA[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=606)


Estimands Use treatment policy for discontinuation as primary, with post-discontinuation follow-up. Prespecify hypothetical estimands as supplementary. Document any region-specific estimand in the protocol and one integrated SAP. EMA diabetes and depression[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=27)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=334) ; FDA obesity[634](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=634) ; Wegovy[678](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=678) ; E17[571](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-vs-ema-pivotal-trial-design-where-expectations?showSourceNumber=571)

#### Bottom line


The FDA–EMA divergence is about how much uncertainty each agency will accept, not about method. The precedents show that FDA is more willing to approve on a single-arm response rate, on a biomarker reasonably likely to predict benefit, or on an integrated or anatomical endpoint whose clinical meaning it judges plausible. EMA more often asks for randomized concurrent control, a comparison with standard of care and directly observed patient-relevant benefit. Programs that build the stricter EU expectations into the global design from the start are less likely to need late protocol amendments or extra studies. (The Leqembi and Kisunla re-examinations turned mainly on the clinical relevance of the effect and on benefit-risk by ApoE4 status, not on comparator or estimand design.) Those expectations are three-arm or mixed comparator portfolios, protected functional key secondaries, and treatment-policy estimands with full follow-up.
